etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: From Late Latin apostata, from Ancient Greek ἀποστάτης (apostátēs, “rebel”), from ἀφίστημι (aphístēmi, “to withdraw, revolt”), from ἀπό (apó, “from”) + ἵστημι (hístēmi, “to stand”).
senses: Exhibiting apostasy; (from the religious viewpoint) guilty of apostasy.
(countable, religion) A person who has renounced a religion or faith.
